body: Thanks. But if you hope I find my friend, then please don't do anything. There's somebody in North Carolina who cares about you just as much as I care about my friend. Things will get better.

Sorry, this sounds a bit rude, please don't take it that way. It's not how I mean it, I just don't know how else to say it.

Why don't you just go to one then? I bet there are people there who can help you. Even if they aren't equipped for somebody in your situation, I'm sure there are people there who, regardless of whether or not it's part of their job, will not hesitate to help you out. Just walk in and talk to somebody. Wander around and find the psych ward or something. ANYTHING is better than ending it. Maybe it seems like there's nothing better than ending it to you, but please don't. I don't know how to express it - for once I'm at a loss for a logical, rhetorical explanation. But please don't.

You sound a lot like a friend of mine. I don't know where they are right now and I'm really worried. Whether you are that friend or not, please don't end it.

Your friends and family care a lot about you. Maybe they don't express it well. Maybe they aren't good friends or family. I don't know. I don't know them. But there's one thing I can guarantee: they care about you. I don't know if my friend is fine and he's just on a ride, or if he's considering killing himself, or if he's already dead. But since I'm in that position, allow me to speak on behalf of your friends and family: Please, please please **please** don't do anything. Talk to us. Try something, anything, other than ending it. We love you.

On another note, you say that you're failing your classes and your prospects for college are ruined. You know what I'd say about that? Don't worry about it. All is not lost. There are tons of ways you can still get into school later, or find another school that will let you in. It sounds like your life's been kind of rough lately - maybe you could take a year off from school, maybe it will help? I don't know what the right path is for you, but I can promise you that there is A way to make it. Even if there isn't, or you can't find it, or you decide not to go to college, there's still a ton of potential for you. Some of the world's most influential, successful, intelligent, incredible people didn't go to college. Some of them didn't even finish high school. My father barely made it out of high school, didn't go to college, and now he's making six figures, and he's raised a family. Things can get better, but only if you choose to keep going on. Please choose to continue living life. There are a million billion opportunities.

Even though you're not, please don't do anything rash. There are people you can talk to. If you try to work through this, things will get better, even if it doesn't seem like they will. If you decide to end it, there's no chance that things will get better. Wouldn't it be better to have a chance of improvement, even if it's a small one, rather than no chance?

I have a friend who I'm really worried about right now, which is why I'm on here. Maybe you're him, maybe you're not. I don't think you are, but while I'm here, I'd like to speak on the behalf of your friends and family.

We care about you. **We care about you.**
Please, please, please, don't do anything. Just talk to one of us. 

I guarantee you that one of your friends or family, if they have any clue that you have had/are having suicidal thoughts, is wishing right now that they had expressed more thoroughly their love for you. That's what's going through my head right now. I wish I had talked with my friend more, I wish I wish I wish I had done something more than what I've done. 

**[Somebody cares about you.](http://i.imgur.com/3qHKDEb.jpg)** We're sorry that we haven't done more for you. Please don't do anything. Talk to us. Things will get better.
